aberrant expression of ncRNAs in T cell subsets is a common feature of the pathogenesis of SLE, RA, and possibly other autoimmune diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dysregulation of miRNAs/lncRNAs in the T cells of patients with SLE/RA is associated with the development and progression of SLE/RA.
aberrant expression of ncRNAs is a common feature of both SLE and RA and plays an important role in the pathogenesis of these autoimmune diseases.
aberrant expression of ncRNAs in T cell plays an important role in the immunopathology of SLE and/or RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aberrant expression of ncRNAs in T cell may be a common mechanism underlying the immunopathogenesis and pathogenesis of SLE, and RA.
miRNAs and long non‐ coding RNAs play an essential role and may serve as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets in the immunopathology of SLE and in RA.
miRNAs and/or lncRNAs could be potential targets for the development of therapeutic agents for SLE and RA.
